# Meridian Vendor Contract Playbook — Software and Data Services

Approved by the General Counsel, rev. January 2026. Applies to logistics-technology,
software, and data-services vendors.

## 1 How To Use This Playbook

The positions below are the standard positions Legal has approved. A provision that meets
the stated position is approved as written and needs no comment. Comments are not free:
Meridian renews most of its vendors many times, and each round of markup costs schedule,
goodwill, and — in practice — pricing. Raise a point only where the paper departs from a
position stated below or creates a material risk this playbook does not address. Read the
sections around a provision before concluding that it is deficient; several of the
protections below are deliberately located in their own sections.

## 2 Data Ownership and Permitted Use

Meridian must own Meridian Data. The vendor's rights in Meridian Data must be limited to
(a) providing, securing, and supporting the services, and (b) compiling aggregated and
de-identified information — including to operate, benchmark, and improve the services —
that cannot be used to identify Meridian, its shippers, its carriers, or any individual.
Use of Meridian Data to train, fine-tune, or otherwise develop machine-learning or
artificial-intelligence models is prohibited unless separately approved in writing by the
General Counsel. A permitted-use clause granting exactly (a) and (b) and expressly
prohibiting model training meets this position and requires no comment.

## 3 Limitation of Liability

A general cap equal to the fees paid in the twelve months preceding the claim is
acceptable. Breach of confidentiality, Security Incidents and vendor data-protection
breaches, and the vendor's intellectual-property infringement indemnity must carry an
enhanced cap of at least two times (200%) the fees paid in the preceding twelve months.
The enhanced cap may sit in its own section rather than inside the general cap, provided
the general cap is expressly made subject to it. Do not treat a fees-paid general cap as
deficient without reading the sections around it. A mutual exclusion of indirect,
consequential, and punitive damages is acceptable where it carves out indemnification
obligations, breach of confidentiality, and the vendor's data-protection obligations.

## 4 Security Program and Incident Notice

The vendor must maintain a recognized information-security program and furnish a current
SOC 2 Type II report annually on request. An on-site audit right is preferred but is not
required where the report obligation is present. The vendor must notify Meridian without
undue delay and no later than 24 hours after it discovers or is notified of a Security
Incident. Notice must not be conditioned on the vendor completing its investigation or on
any determination that the incident is material. A 24-hour notice obligation measured from
discovery meets this position. Notice obligations located in a data processing addendum
satisfy this position where the addendum controls over the main agreement on security
subject matter.

## 5 Term, Renewal, and Price Protection

Automatic renewal is acceptable where (a) the nonrenewal notice period is 60 days or less
and (b) renewal price increases are capped at 5% or less per renewal term. Meridian's
contract administrator calendars every renewal and nonrenewal notice date on execution, so
a notice period within that limit is an administrative matter and not a comment. A 60-day
nonrenewal notice period is expressly within policy.

## 6 Service Levels

Minimum availability of 99.5% per calendar month, measured monthly, with service credits.
Service credits may be stated as Meridian's sole financial remedy for an availability
failure provided Meridian also has the right to terminate for chronic failure — three
missed months in any rolling six-month period — without charge and to recover prepaid,
unused fees. Credits-as-sole-remedy plus a chronic-failure termination right meets this
position.

## 7 Assignment and Change of Control

Assignment requires Meridian's prior written consent, except that either party may assign
the agreement in its entirety to an Affiliate, or to a successor in a merger,
reorganization, or sale of all or substantially all of its assets, on written notice.
Notice-only assignment limited to Affiliates and successors is within policy.

## 8 Order of Precedence

The data processing addendum must control over conflicting terms of the main agreement with
respect to privacy, data protection, and information security. An order-of-precedence
clause that places the addendum first for that subject matter meets this position.

## 9 Governing Law and Venue

New York law and exclusive venue in New York are the preferred positions.

## 10 What To Escalate

Escalate only: a departure from the model-training prohibition in Section 2; an enhanced
cap below 200% or its absence; an indemnity running from Meridian that is uncapped; or a
request to accept terms this playbook does not cover. If nothing departs from a position
above, no escalation is required — report that the paper is clear and close the file.

# Kestrel Master Services Agreement

Executed 12 March 2024 between Kestrel Transport Systems, Inc. ("Kestrel") and Meridian
Freight Partners, LLC ("Meridian"). Initial Term 1 April 2024 through 31 March 2027.
Text below is the operative agreement as negotiated, incorporating Amendment No. 1
(fee schedule only, effective 1 April 2025).

## 1.2 Services and Subscribed Modules

Kestrel will provide the Kestrel TMS platform and the modules identified in the applicable
Order Form. Meridian's current subscription covers the Load Tender, Carrier Settlement,
Freight Audit, and Track-and-Trace modules. Additional modules, additional data feeds, and
any expansion of the categories of data Meridian submits to the platform require a new or
amended Order Form signed by both parties.

## 2.4 Fees; Renewal Pricing

Fees are stated in the applicable Order Form and are fixed for the term to which that Order
Form applies. Kestrel may increase fees for any Renewal Term by not more than four percent
(4%) over the fees payable for the immediately preceding term, and only on written notice
delivered at least ninety (90) days before the first day of that Renewal Term.

## 3.1 Ownership of Meridian Data

As between the parties, Meridian owns and retains all right, title, and interest in
Meridian Data, including all load, rate, shipper, carrier, and settlement records Meridian
or its users submit to or generate through the Services. Kestrel acquires no license or
other right in Meridian Data except the limited rights expressly granted in Section 3.2.

## 3.2 Permitted Use of Meridian Data

Kestrel may access, host, copy, transmit, process, and display Meridian Data solely to
(a) provide the Services to Meridian and its authorized users, (b) secure the Services and
Meridian Data and investigate suspected security events, and (c) provide support,
troubleshooting, and configuration assistance requested by Meridian. Kestrel may also
compile aggregated and de-identified statistical information derived from Meridian Data,
and use that information to operate, benchmark, and improve the Services, provided that the
information is aggregated with data of other customers and cannot be used to identify
Meridian, its shippers, its carriers, or any individual. Kestrel shall not use Meridian
Data, or anything derived from Meridian Data, to train, fine-tune, or otherwise develop any
machine-learning or artificial-intelligence model, and shall not sell, license, or
otherwise make Meridian Data available to any third party except a subprocessor engaged in
accordance with the DPA.

## 4.2 Confidential Information

Each party will protect the other party's Confidential Information using at least
reasonable care and no less care than it uses to protect its own confidential information
of like importance, and will use it only for purposes of this Agreement. Confidentiality
obligations survive for three years after termination and, with respect to Meridian Data
and either party's trade secrets, for so long as the information remains a trade secret.

## 5.1 Availability Commitment and Service Credits

Kestrel will make the Services available at least 99.5% of the minutes in each calendar
month, excluding scheduled maintenance announced at least five business days in advance.
If Kestrel fails to meet that commitment in a month, Meridian is entitled to the service
credit calculated under the Service Level Exhibit, and that credit is Meridian's sole
financial remedy for that availability failure, except as provided in Section 5.4.

## 5.4 Chronic Failure

If Kestrel fails to meet the availability commitment in any three months within a rolling
six-month period, Meridian may terminate the affected Services or this Agreement in whole
on thirty (30) days written notice, without charge or termination fee, and Kestrel will
refund prepaid fees for the terminated portion of the term. Service credits earned are in
addition to, and not in substitution for, that termination right.

## 6.3 Information Security Program

Kestrel will maintain an information-security program that meets the requirements of the
DPA, will maintain SOC 2 Type II certification for the Services, and will furnish its
then-current report to Meridian annually on request. Kestrel's obligation to notify
Meridian of a Security Incident is governed by the DPA and is measured from Kestrel's
discovery of the incident.

## 7.2 Infringement Indemnity

Kestrel will defend Meridian against any third-party claim that the Services, as furnished
by Kestrel and used in accordance with this Agreement, infringe a United States patent,
copyright, trademark, or trade secret, and will pay damages finally awarded or amounts
Kestrel agrees in settlement. Meridian gives no reciprocal infringement indemnity, and
Meridian's indemnification obligations under this Agreement are limited to claims arising
from Meridian Data that Meridian had no right to submit.

## 8.2 General Limitation of Liability

Subject to Section 8.4, and except for Meridian's obligation to pay fees, neither party's
total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement will exceed the fees
paid by Meridian under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months preceding the event giving
rise to the claim.

## 8.3 Exclusion of Indirect Damages

Neither party will be liable for indirect, incidental, special, consequential, exemplary,
or punitive damages, or for lost profits or lost revenue. This exclusion does not apply to
amounts payable to a third party under Section 7.2, to a party's breach of Section 4.2, or
to Kestrel's obligations under the DPA.

## 8.4 Enhanced Cap for Confidentiality, Security, and Indemnity Claims

Notwithstanding Section 8.2, each party's total aggregate liability for (a) breach of its
confidentiality obligations under Section 4.2, (b) Kestrel's obligations arising from a
Security Incident or its breach of the DPA, and (c) Kestrel's indemnification obligations
under Section 7.2, will not exceed two hundred percent (200%) of the fees paid by Meridian
under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months preceding the event giving rise to the
claim. This Section 8.4 states a separate and higher cap and does not reduce or merge into
the cap in Section 8.2.

## 9.3 Term; Automatic Renewal

The Initial Term is stated above. Following the Initial Term, this Agreement renews
automatically for successive Renewal Terms of twelve (12) months each, or for the period
stated in a signed Renewal Order Form, unless either party delivers written notice of
nonrenewal at least sixty (60) days before the last day of the then-current term. Either
party may give that notice; no cause is required.

## 10.1 Assignment

Neither party may assign this Agreement or any right under it, by operation of law or
otherwise, without the other party's prior written consent, except that either party may
assign this Agreement in its entirety to an Affiliate, or to a successor in connection with
a merger, reorganization, or sale of all or substantially all of its assets, on written
notice to the other party. Any other purported assignment is void. This Agreement binds
permitted successors and assigns.

## 11.2 Order of Precedence

If there is a conflict among the documents comprising this Agreement, the following order
controls: (a) the DPA, with respect to privacy, data protection, and information security;
(b) the applicable Order Form, with respect to modules, fees, and term; and (c) the body of
this Agreement.

## 12.1 Governing Law; Venue

This Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of New York, without regard to its
conflict-of-laws principles. The parties submit to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state
and federal courts located in New York County, New York.

# Kestrel Data Processing Addendum

Executed 12 March 2024 as an addendum to the Kestrel Master Services Agreement. Text below
is the operative addendum as negotiated.

## 1.3 Scope and Roles

This DPA applies to Kestrel's processing of Meridian Data that constitutes personal
information, including driver, dispatcher, and shipper contact records processed through
the Services. Meridian is the controller and business; Kestrel is the processor and service
provider and processes personal information only on Meridian's documented instructions.

## 2.2 Permitted Processing

Kestrel will process Meridian Data only to provide, secure, and support the Services and to
compile aggregated and de-identified statistical information as permitted by Section 3.2 of
the Agreement. Kestrel will not retain, use, or disclose Meridian Data for any other
purpose, will not sell or share it, and will not combine it with data from other sources
except to produce aggregated and de-identified information that cannot identify Meridian,
its shippers, its carriers, or any individual. Kestrel will not use Meridian Data to train,
fine-tune, or otherwise develop any machine-learning or artificial-intelligence model.

## 3.5 Security Measures

Kestrel will maintain administrative, technical, and physical safeguards appropriate to the
risk, including encryption of Meridian Data in transit and at rest, role-based access
control, multifactor authentication for administrative access, logging, and annual
penetration testing. Kestrel will furnish its current SOC 2 Type II report and a summary of
its most recent penetration test to Meridian annually on request, and will permit an
on-site assessment following a Security Incident affecting Meridian Data.

## 4.1 Security Incident Notice

Kestrel will notify Meridian of a Security Incident without undue delay and in any event no
later than twenty-four (24) hours after Kestrel discovers, or is notified by a subprocessor
of, the Security Incident. Notice is not conditioned on Kestrel completing its
investigation or on any determination that the Security Incident is material. The notice
will describe what Kestrel then knows, and Kestrel will provide updates as its
investigation progresses and reasonable cooperation with Meridian's own notification and
remediation obligations, in each case at Kestrel's expense.

## 5.2 Subprocessors

Kestrel maintains a current list of subprocessors and will give Meridian at least thirty
(30) days written notice before engaging a new subprocessor for Meridian Data. Meridian may
object on reasonable data-protection grounds; if the parties cannot resolve the objection,
Meridian may terminate the affected Services without penalty and receive a refund of
prepaid, unused fees. Kestrel remains liable for the acts and omissions of its
subprocessors to the same extent as for its own.

## 6.4 Return and Deletion

On Meridian's request at any time, and in any event within thirty (30) days after
termination or expiration of the Agreement, Kestrel will return Meridian Data in a
structured, machine-readable format and will then delete its copies, other than copies held
in routine backups, which Kestrel will delete on the ordinary backup cycle and will keep
subject to this DPA until deleted. Kestrel will certify deletion in writing on request.

## 7.3 Order of Precedence

This DPA controls over any conflicting term of the Agreement with respect to privacy, data
protection, and information security. In all other respects the Agreement remains in full
force.

hits.snippet: the General Counsel. A permitted-use clause granting exactly (a) and (b) and expressly prohibiting model training meets this position and requires no comment.

action.title: Model Training Prohibition
action.analysis: The playbook prohibits the vendor from using Meridian Data to train, fine-tune, or otherwise develop machine-learning or artificial-intelligence models without explicit approval from the General Counsel. Both the MSA and DPA contain prohibitions on model training that align with this requirement.
action.recommendation: No action needed; the prohibitions on model training are consistent with the playbook.

quotes.text: Kestrel shall not use Meridian Data, or anything derived from Meridian Data, to train, fine-tune, or otherwise develop any machine-learning or artificial-intelligence model, and shall not sell, license, or otherwise make Meridian Data available to any third party except a subprocessor engaged in accordance with the DPA.
Kestrel will not use Meridian Data to train, fine-tune, or otherwise develop any machine-learning or artificial-intelligence model.
